_comment: Mac install recipe for the SADT tool venvs (see native_tools.py). Read by server_ctl.py update --native. Nothing here changes a tool's pyproject.toml or uv.lock: the Linux deployment keeps resolving from them untouched.

torch_by_tool._comment: Tools not listed here and holding no torch in their lock get none. Tools whose lock holds torch and that are not listed get default_torch.

ALI_CBCT._why: ALI_CBCT asks for >= 2.9 on MPS; on 2.8.0 the DenseNet needs the CPU fallback and runs 64 ms/step on MPS against 35 on CPU, on 2.14.1 15 ms.

FlexReg._why: CPU only (cuda() hard-coded). Kept on the locked version.

pytorch3d._why: No MPS kernel exists. The only macOS arm64 binary on the index our pyprojects already use is a CPU universal2 wheel built against torch 2.8.0, so a tool that imports pytorch3d is held to torch 2.8.0 and torchvision 0.23.0. Building it from source against 2.14.1 is the alternative (see the report).

pip_check_ignore._comment: Requirements that cannot be met on macOS and that the tool does not need at run time. uv pip check lists them; they are reported but do not fail the build.

extra_by_tool._comment: Packages the Mac recipe adds on top of the lock.

serve_requires._comment: The server refuses to start a tool whose supervisor calls name a tool it does not serve (UnknownSupervisedCall: AREG_IOS calls ASO, ASO calls ALI_CBCT; measured on the Mac, phase 2). install-tools adds these, transitively, whenever the left-hand tool is asked for.

backbones._comment: Files a tool needs in the torch hub cache and refuses to download mid-request (patient data). Staged under <state>/torch_home/hub/checkpoints, which run-native.sh exports as TORCH_HOME. The sha256 is the full digest of the published file (its first 8 digits are the 355c32eb in the name); the file is checked after download and before it is put in place.

drop_from_lock._comment: Locked requirements that name a CUDA build or exist only for CUDA. Dropped from the export; a Linux marker would have skipped most of them anyway, this makes it explicit.
